26 Two waves, P and Q, meet at a point X and superpose.
Initially, the two waves meet at X in phase (zero phase difference) so that the resultant wave has
an amplitude of 14.0 cm at that point.
The phase difference between the two waves is then changed so that they meet at X with a
phase difference of 180°. The resultant wave now has an amplitude of 4.0 cm at X.
What is the amplitude of one of the waves at point X?
A
2.0 cm
B
5.0 cm
C
10 cm
D
18 cm

hints: Notice the two resultant amplitudes at X: $14.0\text{ cm}$ for zero phase difference and $4.0\text{ cm}$ for $180^{\circ}$ phase difference.
Recall how superposition combines individual amplitudes $a_P$ and $a_Q$ for constructive interference in phase and destructive interference in antiphase.
Set up $a_P + a_Q = 14.0\text{ cm}$ and $|a_P - a_Q| = 4.0\text{ cm}$, then solve the pair of equations for the smaller amplitude.
walkthrough: Let the amplitudes of P and Q at X be $a_P$ and $a_Q$. Both are positive quantities in $\text{cm}$.
In phase, zero phase difference, the displacements add at every instant, so resultant amplitude is the sum: $a_P + a_Q = 14.0\text{ cm}$.
With $180^{\circ}$ phase difference, one displacement is positive when the other is negative, so resultant amplitude is the magnitude of the difference: $|a_P - a_Q| = 4.0\text{ cm}$.
Adding the two equations for the larger amplitude $a_{max}$: $2a_{max} = 14.0 + 4.0 = 18.0$, so $a_{max} = 9.0\text{ cm}$.
Subtracting gives the smaller amplitude: $2a_{min} = 14.0 - 4.0 = 10.0$, so $a_{min} = 5.0\text{ cm}$. Check: $9.0 + 5.0 = 14.0$ and $9.0 - 5.0 = 4.0$.
The listed value $5.0\text{ cm}$ is one of the two wave amplitudes. This is option B.

A.explanation: Half of $4.0\text{ cm}$ is not the wave amplitude. In antiphase the resultant is the difference, not half the difference.

B.explanation: Amplitudes $9.0\text{ cm}$ and $5.0\text{ cm}$ give sum $14.0\text{ cm}$ in phase and difference $4.0\text{ cm}$ in antiphase.

C.explanation: Adding $4.0\text{ cm}$ to $14.0\text{ cm}$ then halving gives $9.0\text{ cm}$, not $10\text{ cm}$, and $10\text{ cm}$ does not satisfy both conditions.

D.explanation: Adding $14.0\text{ cm}$ and $4.0\text{ cm}$ gives $18\text{ cm}$, which is the sum of the two resultants, not one wave amplitude.
